records.text: Intervention effect. Base system: fcc phase of FeCoNiTi (Fe21.3Co24.8Ni32.2Ti21.6). Intervention: Extracted magnetization curves of fcc phase by subtracting C14 contribution. Processing: Calculated M(H) of fcc phase using equation: M_fcc = (M_FeCoNiTi - f_C14 * M_C14-dominant) / f_fcc. Test conditions: Isothermal magnetization at 50, 100, 200, 300, 400 K. item.intervention: Performed electronic structure calculations using CPA-KKR method
item.processing: Akai-KKR program, PBE exchange-correlation potential, spin-polarization and spin-orbit interaction included
item.test_conditions: Theoretical calculation at 0 K, using experimental lattice parameters and EDX compositions
item.structure_change: Calculated ferromagnetic ground state for fcc phase; Ti moment antiparallel to Fe, Co, Ni
item.property_change: Theoretical Ms = 78.6 emu/g; experimental Ms at 50 K = 43 emu/g; theoretical spin moments: Fe=2.254 μB, Co=1.285 μB, Ni=0.341 μB, Ti=-0.426 μB
item.attributed_mechanism: The discrepancy between theoretical and experimental Ms suggests the presence of a spin-canted component
quotes: Electronic structure calculations were also executed utilizing the coherent potential approximation (CPA) approach.

item.intervention: Measured temperature-dependent DC magnetization from 50 to 1150 K
item.processing: VersaLab apparatus (50–400 K), VSM (400–1150 K), external field 100 Oe
item.structure_change: Three ferromagnetic transitions identified at 1084 K, 214 K, and 168 K via derivative of χdc
item.property_change: χdc sharply rises around 1100 K, plateau to ~300 K, then second increase; Tc values: 1084 K, 214 K, 168 K
item.attributed_mechanism: Local minima of dχdc/dT define Tc values; multiple FM phases explain the transitions
quotes: The temperature-dependent DC magnetization χdc(T) ranging from 50 to 400 K was recorded utilizing the VersaLab apparatus (Quantum Design).
As the temperature decreases from 1150 K, χdc sharply rises around 1100 K, followed by a plateau extending to approximately 300 K.
